newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS SWAMP PITIFUL MAVERICKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS SWAMP PITIFUL MAVERICKS.

text.p: John Starks scored 17 of his 21 points in the first half, when the New York Knicks limited the Dallas Mavericks to franchise lows for points and field goals, in a 102-72 victory on Tuesday.
The Mavericks tied all-time team lows with just eight baskets and 28 points in the first half, enduring field-goal droughts of 9:30 and 6:19.
"We had a pretty good week of preparation with the hope that we would play better, but you can't shoot the ball like that in the first half and expect to survive against a quality basketball team."
In Atlanta, Henry James' desperation three-pointer with one second left in overtime took the Atlanta Hawks to their 12th straight home win, 105-103 over the Phoenix Suns.
With 5.3 seconds to go, Atlanta worked the ball in to James at the top of the three-point arc. He squared up and, with Kevin Johnson in his face, buried the game-winning basket.
The Suns had a chance to win it, but Wesley Person's three-pointer bounced off the front of the rim at the buzzer.
In Detroit, Vin Baker had 25 points and Sherman Douglas scored five in a 13-2 fourth-quarter run as the Milwaukee Bucks ended a five-game losing streak with an 86-76 victory over the Detroit Pistons.
Ray Allen added 19 points and Glenn Robinson 18 for Milwaukee. Grant Hill scored 24 points for Detroit.
In Indiana, Dale Davis scored a season-high 21 points as the Indiana Pacers welcomed centre Rik Smits back to the lineup by rallying for a 95-90 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Travis Best scored 15 of his 19 points in the fourth quarter.
Terrell Brandon scored 26 points for Cleveland.

In Minnesota, Clyde Drexler poured in a season-high 37 points and Xakeem Olajuwon scored 12 of his 22 in the fourth quarter as the Houston Rockets rallied for a 104-95 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Stephon Marbury's layup with 4:08 remaining pulled the Timberwolves within 87-86, but the Rockets reeled off the next seven points for a 94-86 lead with 73 seconds to play.

At New Jersey, Jayson Williams returned from a 10-game absence with 19 points and 16 rebounds and Kerry Kittles keyed a decisive third-quarter run with a pair of three-pointers, leading the New Jersey Nets to an 90-74 victory over the undermanned San Antonio Spurs.
Kendall had 16 points and Shawn Bradley added 15 for the Nets.
In Seattle, Gary Payton scored 30 points, including six during an 18-5 run straddling the third and fourth quarters, as the Seattle SuperSonics pulled away for a 94-85 victory over the Miami Heat.
Detlef Schrempf added 19 points and Sam Perkins hit four three-pointers in the fourth quarter to finish with 18 for Seattle.

In Toronto, Loy Vaught scored nine of his 21 points in the fourth quarter as the Los Angeles Clippers overcame a 14-point deficit to post their fourth straight victory, 87-80 over the Toronto Raptors.
Vaught, who added 14 rebounds, hit a jumper early in the final period to spark a 9-0 run that put the Clippers ahead to stay.

In Orlando, Anfernee Hardaway and Nick Anderson returned to the lineup as the Orlando Magic used their best starting five for the first time this season and cruised to an easy 109-88 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers.
Hardaway had 15 points and seven rebounds in his first game since December 18th. Anderson had 12 points, eight rebounds and five assists in his first game in a month.
In Sacramento, LaPhonso Ellis scored 33 points and Mark Jackson had 22 points and 12 assists as the Denver Nuggets stopped a four-game losing streak with a 109-96 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
Dale Ellis added 21 points for the Nuggets. Mitch Richmond scored 19 points and Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf added 18 off the bench for the Nuggets.
